text:
Maya (CEO): quick follow-up from today's all-hands for anyone who missed it — dropping Q&A about the customer wins/losses segment here
Liam (Head of Sales): two quick datapoints: one win where we beat on reliability in a pilot, one loss where procurement flagged pricing vs self-hosted options
Elena (Customer Success): add: customers who stayed signed up because we helped with their eval harness, not just infra specs
Sam P. (VP Product): curious re: reliability win 14 what did we actually do differently vs. the competitor?
Rohit (Solutions Eng): short answer: we pre-warmed KV caches for the demo, pinned a smaller Dedicated pool to reduce cold-starts, and used a slightly higher batch concurrency during peak to smooth tail latency
Anya (PM): product question: should we make pre-warm/pinning a config customers can toggle in Dedicated?
Maya (CEO): yes, but expose it carefully. customers want control but not complexity. maybe a toggle with three presets: balanced / latency-priority / cost-priority
Liam (Head of Sales): from demos: 'latency-priority' is a sweet spot for enterprise RFPs. they will pay a premium for predictable 99.9% tail
Elena (Customer Success): on the other hand, small teams are very price-sensitive. they liked our docs for "cheap eval" but still picked cheaper self-hosted quantized stacks in two cases last quarter
Sam P. (VP Product): idea: publish two short artifacts: 1) "Latency profile & what it means" (public-facing), 2) "Starter dedicated guide" (sales + small customers). both should include tradeoffs and config examples
Rohit (Solutions Eng): example route policy snippet we keep showing in demos:
```
route_policy:
  preset: latency-priority
  prewarm_kv: true
  min_pool_size: 2
  max_concurrency: 8
```
Elena (Customer Success): also ask: can we formalize "eval assistance" as a billable add-on? that closed several deals last quarter
LegalBot: FYI: any contract language for add-on services needs scope and SLA caps. recommend a standard 10-20 hour engagement template
Maya (CEO): we can offer a scoped eval add-on. set expectations: e.g., 12 eng hours, one integration call, one-week turnaround for basic evals
Anya (PM): I will draft the Starter Dedicated one-pager and the latency-profile doc. timeline: draft by next Tues, final by end of week. assigning Sam to review latency doc + Legal for add-on wording
Liam (Head of Sales): will share a couple anonymized RFP quotes to help frame pricing tiers (DMing now)
Sam P. (VP Product): small roadmap tweak: bump pre-warm/pinning UX up one sprint, and include telemetry to show customers "why your tail spiked" in Console
Rohit (Solutions Eng): please include a short appendix in the one-pager about tokenization gotchas and prompt length effects on tail latency
Elena (Customer Success): and a checklist for evaluation data hygiene and privacy redaction — customers appreciated that in previous wins
Maya (CEO): great. final ask: can someone make a 1-slide summary that Sales can use in calls?
Anya (PM): yes, will do a 1-slide cheat sheet for Sales + CS (lead with: why customers buy us, what to offer as add-ons, and 3 config examples). ETA Wed AM
Liam (Head of Sales): thanks 44D will test the slide in two upcoming demos
Maya (CEO): thanks team. post any follow-ups here and tag Anya. we will review progress in leadership sync next week :sparkles:
